title: The tree of Zaqqum is named.
subtitle: The surah turns to those who denied the meeting
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah here tells {trap}how He will punish the disbelievers who deny the meeting with Him{/trap}. Some commentators applied it to Abu Jahl; Ibn Kathir says he is included, but it is not only about him.
now: A road sign shows a sharp bend ahead. It is not there to frighten you. {idea}It is there so you slow down in time.{/idea} Descriptions of the Fire work the same way.
old: Verses about the Fire are only meant to frighten.
new: The warning is described so I can steer away while there is time.
try: Name one habit you know is heading the wrong way and make one small turn today.

title: It is the food of the one who sinned.
subtitle: What a life of wrongdoing feeds on
then: Ibn Kathir says the sinner here is one who {trap}sinned by words and deeds{/trap}. Abu ad-Darda' corrected a man who misheard the word as orphan: say {trap}the food of the evildoer{/trap}, meaning he will have no other food.
now: The shows you binge, the gossip you swallow in the group chat, the money you earn in a grey way. {idea}What you feed your soul now is a kind of food too.{/idea}
old: What I consume day to day does not really affect me.
new: What I take in now shapes where I end up.
try: Skip one thing today you know feeds the worst in you, and replace it with something good.

title: Like dregs of oil, it churns inside.
subtitle: Food that harms instead of nourishing
then: Ibn Kathir explains the word as {trap}like the dregs of oil{/trap}. It boils in the bellies {trap}because of its heat and rancidity{/trap}. It is food that gives nothing and only hurts.
now: The angry message you sent felt good for ten seconds. Then it sat in your stomach all night. {idea}Some things taste fine going down and churn afterwards.{/idea}
old: If it feels good now, it cannot be that bad.
new: Wrong that feels good now can turn bitter inside me.
try: Before you react today, ask: how will this feel in an hour? Then choose.

title: Boiling like scalding water.
subtitle: No cooling, no comfort

row.title: seek refuge now
sub: ask to be kept from it

then: The image completes the last verse: the food boils inside {trap}like the boiling of scalding water{/trap}. Ibn Kathir keeps the explanation short. The picture is meant to be enough.
now: You pull your hand back from a kettle without thinking. Your body knows to avoid harm. {idea}The verse asks your heart to learn the same reflex.{/idea}
old: I can deal with these warnings some other time.
new: My heart should flinch from the Fire the way my hand flinches from heat.
try: Ask Allah tonight to protect you and your family from the Fire.

title: Seize him and drag him to the middle.
subtitle: The proud are taken without a say
then: The order is given to the keepers of Hell. Mujahid said it means {trap}take him and push him{/trap}, into the middle of the Fire. The one who did as he pleased now has no say at all.
now: Right now you decide when to wake, what to eat, whether to pray. That freedom feels permanent. {idea}It is the window in which choices still count.{/idea}
old: I will always be in charge of my own choices.
new: My freedom to choose is a window, and it closes.
try: Use your freedom today to choose one good thing you have been putting off.

title: Then pour over his head the boiling torment.
subtitle: A sober picture of what denial reaches
then: The punishment continues: {trap}pour over his head the torment of boiling water{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to a similar verse in Surah al-Hajj and adds a short prayer: {reward}may Allah protect us from that{/reward}.
now: You want to scroll past this verse quickly. That is fine to feel. {reward}Do what Ibn Kathir did: stop and ask Allah to protect you.{/reward}
new: Hard verses are a cue to pause and ask for protection.
try: When you reach a verse about the Fire, stop and say: Allah, protect me from it.

title: Taste it, you who thought yourself mighty and noble.
subtitle: The status he claimed, said back to him
then: The keepers of Hell say this {trap}by way of ridicule and rebuke{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said it means: {trap}you are neither mighty nor generous{/trap}. The titles he carried in this world are handed back to him empty.
now: The job title on your email signature. The family name people respect. The way the room quiets when you speak. {idea}None of these titles is checked on the Day. Only what you did is.{/idea}
old: My standing among people says something about my worth.
new: Titles end at the grave. My deeds are my only rank.
try: Do one humble task today you would normally leave to someone else.

title: This is what you used to doubt.
subtitle: The doubt from verse nine, answered
then: The surah began by saying they {trap}play about in doubt{/trap}. Here it closes the loop: {trap}this is what you used to doubt{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to: this is the Fire which you used to deny, is this magic, or do you not see?
now: You put off reading the letter from the bank because you suspect what it says. Not opening it does not change the number. {idea}Doubt only delays the moment you see it.{/idea}
old: As long as I am not sure, I do not have to act.
new: My doubt will end either way. Better it ends now, by choice.
try: Settle one question you have been doubting by asking someone knowledgeable this week.
